how_to_add_a_plane: Read a source that states how the auth method bills, not just where its model ids route. Record the source, who established the claim and when, and a review date 60 days later. A ruleless quota proxy is still a billing claim and needs its own provenance and review.

planes.note: Kimi states: 'Kimi Code is the developer-focused AI coding service within Kimi membership benefits, provided together with a Kimi membership subscription and sharing the same quota. Requests from the CLI, VS Code, Desktop, and third-party tools all count toward that quota.' Its Quota and Limits section states: 'Both groups share the Kimi membership monthly total quota: if the monthly total is reached, Kimi Code quota is frozen until the monthly quota resets or you upgrade.' API Keys share that quota, so apikey does not mean pay-as-you-go for this provider. https://www.kimi.com/en/help/membership/membership-update-rules says credits are deducted based on actual token usage, varying with model, context length, tool calls and plan. No numeric per-token-class quota conversion is established by these pages. Moonshot API rates at each exact moonshotai canonical id are relative quota stand-ins, not subscription charges; an absent API card stays unpriced, never the plan's published zero.

OpenCode Go is a subscription sold as an API key: 'You subscribe to OpenCode Go and get your API key.' The docs list 'Go | $10/month' and 'Go Plus | $40/month', and state: 'Usage limits are defined as monthly dollar amounts. The table below shows the monthly limit for each plan and the token costs for each model. Token pricing is the same for Go and Go Plus.' and 'Each model has the following usage limits: 5-hour — 20% of the monthly limit; weekly — 50%; and monthly — 100%.' https://opencode.ai/go says the same: 'enforced across rolling windows: 20% of the monthly allowance per 5 hours, 50% per week, and 100% per month.' Usage is therefore valued per model at the listed token prices, which are the opencode-go rates models.dev publishes (read 2026-10-22: GLM-5.3 $1.40 input, $4.40 output, $0.26 cached read per 1M on both). Those rates are relative quota weights against a flat subscription, not amounts billed, so rates_from_provider names opencode-go itself and nothing is borrowed. The Go plan's per-model monthly limits (for example $15 for GPT 6 Luna and Kimi K3, $60 for Kimi K2.7 Code and GLM-5.3-Flash, Unlimited for LongCat 2.5 Preview Free and Beam Free) are quota limits, not prices, and are not encoded as rates. With Extra usage turned on, Go 'will fall back to your pay-as-you-go balance after you've reached your usage limits'; those calls are billed, and this plane cannot tell them apart. The pricing table's Cached Write column shows '-' for most models and states no billing rule, so no class rule is curated.

planes.source_ref: Probes with the operator's Meta coding-plan login (vault credential oauth:meta) on 2026-10-13: GET https://api.meta.ai/v1/models at 16:42:35Z returned 200 with 12 ids including muse-wonder-full-1.0; POST https://api.meta.ai/v1/responses with muse-wonder-full-1.0 at 16:42:45Z returned 200.
planes.note: Meta's coding plan bills by subscription and publishes no token-class quota rule. API prices are a relative quota stand-in, not an amount billed. The curated Muse Wonder Full row has no API price to borrow and therefore carries no rates.
The Codex rate card says usage is priced based on API token usage. These are relative quota weights, not amounts billed by a ChatGPT subscription.

rules.note: The rate card meters input tokens, cached input tokens and output tokens, with no cache-write class. Cache writes have no separate surcharge; that does not make the input tokens free.

planes.note: Claude Code shares Pro/Max plan limits, and cached portions count less against those limits. The API's discounted cache-read rate reflects that direction, but is a quota proxy rather than a subscription charge. No numeric per-class rule is published.
Prompt-caching usage and pricing gives input and cached-input columns, not a separate write column.

rules.note: Prompt tokens (non-cached) pay the full prompt token price. No write surcharge is stated.

planes.note: The completion API splits prompt usage into cache hit and cache miss, with no write field.

rules.note: Prompt tokens equal prompt_cache_hit_tokens plus prompt_cache_miss_tokens. A cache miss is input, not a free write.
